gap: No result ChatGPT got states an independently measured speed or wow figure for any of its four picks. The only one on record is Thom Moon's test of the Fluance RT81+ for SoundStage! Access, using a phone RPM app: 33.5 rpm at 33⅓ (Moon calls it about 0.55% fast; the 33.5 reading works out to +0.50%) with ±0.17% wow, and 45.16 rpm at 45 (+0.36%) with ±0.21% wow.
standout_why: I compared valveandvinyl.com/turntables/crosley-alternatives (rank 6) and platterandplinth.com/turntables/best-with-preamp (rank 13). Both give wow and flutter and S/N for the AT-LP70X and RT81 as the maker's own figures only, and valveandvinyl says outright that every figure is 'the manufacturer's own published value.' Neither page gives a measured speed, rumble or wow figure from a named reviewer or lab. TechRadar and vinylpickup were not opened (vinylpickup failed with a certificate error), so I can't say whether they have one. None of my searches surfaced a measurement on either site.
decides: This is a supporting fact, not one that changes the pick. ChatGPT's 'hi-fi upgrades' choice, the RT81+, is the only one of its four cards with a named third-party measurement. That test found it running about half a percent fast, inside Fluance's current published ±1.00% speed variation and close to its 0.2% wow and flutter rating. Neither Audio-Technica deck nor the Sony has a named measurement I could find, so for them the page can only quote maker specs. Moon's readings come from a phone app, not lab gear, and the page should say so.

findings.label: Measured speed at 33⅓ rpm (Thom Moon, SoundStage! Access)
findings.source_title: Fluance RT81+ Turntable and Audio-Technica AT-VM95E Cartridge, SoundStage! Access
findings.note: The page says 'Created: 15 February 2024'. Measured with 'the RPM app on my phone'; no test record named. Arithmetic: (33.5 − 33.333) / 33.333 = +0.50%, so the app probably read slightly above 33.5 before rounding. Quote it as 'about 0.5% fast'.

findings.source_title: Fluance RT81+ Turntable and Audio-Technica AT-VM95E Cartridge, SoundStage! Access
findings.note: Phone RPM app estimate, review created 2024-02-15. The reviewer said the speed deviation did not seem to affect the music in his listening.

findings.source_title: Fluance RT81+ Turntable and Audio-Technica AT-VM95E Cartridge, SoundStage! Access
findings.note: Phone RPM app. (45.16 − 45) / 45 = +0.356%, which matches the reviewer's 0.36%.

findings.label: Measured wow at 45 rpm (Thom Moon, SoundStage! Access)
findings.source_title: Fluance RT81+ Turntable and Audio-Technica AT-VM95E Cartridge, SoundStage! Access
findings.note: Phone RPM app estimate. Just above Fluance's 0.2% wow-and-flutter rating.

findings.label: Maker's published speed variation and wow and flutter (for comparison with the measurement)
findings.value: Speed variation ±1.00%; wow and flutter 0.2%; S/N 67 dB or higher (A-weighted, 20 kHz LPF); line output 140 mV
findings.source_title: Fluance RT81+ Elite High Fidelity Vinyl Turntable
findings.note: The 2024 review quoted Fluance's speed-variation claim as ±0.1%. The maker page today says ±1.00%, so the measured +0.5% fits the current spec but not the older one. The page lists $349.99, matching ChatGPT's card.

unsourced: Independent speed, wow, rumble or preamp-noise measurements for the Audio-Technica AT-LP70X and AT-LP70XBT. I searched for Hi-Fi News lab reports (none for these models), Stereophile, Sound & Vision, AudioScienceReview and German magazines. The CNET review is blocked to fetch and the Louder AT-LP70XBT page came back truncated with no figures.
Independent measurements for the Sony PS-LX310BT. The hifi.de test is qualitative only, CHOICE's test scores are paywalled, and I found no ASR or lab report.

Independent measurements for the original Fluance RT81. Thom Moon's 2017 SoundStage review quotes only the maker's 0.2% and 67 dB figures, and TechGearLab (Max Mutter, 2017-12-06) gives 1–10 scores, not figures.
AnalogPlanet's RT81+ page (analogplanet.com/node/125325) returned HTTP 403, so I couldn't check it for measurements.
A Newport Test Labs 'Laboratory Test Report' on Everand (a search snippet implied an AT-LP120XUSB speed test) returned HTTP 404 at both URLs.
